'''William Ssempa Kisaalita''' (born December 15, 1953, in [[Kampala, Uganda]]) is a [[chemical engineer]] and professor of engineering at the [[University of Georgia]].

== Biography ==
Kisaalita was born in [[Kampala, Uganda]]. He completed his Bachelor of Science degree in mechanical engineering at [[Makerere University]] in Kampala, Uganda.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rbc.uga.edu/leaders/Kisaalita.php|title=William S. Kisaalita, Research|website=www.rbc.uga.edu|access-date=2016-10-03|archive-date=2018-03-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180311150413/http://rbc.uga.edu/leaders/Kisaalita.php|url-status=dead}}</ref> He obtained his Ph.D. in chemical engineering in 1987 from the University of British Columbia, Vancouver, B.C., Canada.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://jces.ua.edu/william-kisaalita/|title=William Kisaalita – JCES|website=jces.ua.edu|access-date=2016-10-03|archive-date=2021-10-21|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211021153608/http://jces.ua.edu/william-kisaalita/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He joined the University of Georgia as a professor in 1991.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uga.edu/faculty/profile/william-s.-kisaalita/|title=William S. Kisaalita - Focus On Faculty|date=May 20, 2012|publisher=}}</ref>

== Professional work ==
Kisaalita's primary research area has been in the application of 3D cell cultures in pre-clinical drug discovery. He authored a graduate textbook in this area titled ''3D Cell-Based Biosensors in Drug Discovery Programs''.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kisaalita|first= William S.|title= 3D cell-based biosensors in drug discovery programs: Microtissue engineering for high throughput screening|publisher= CRC Press|year= 2010|isbn= 9781420073508|url= https://books.google.com/books?id=G43LBQAAQBAJ&q=3D+Cell+Culture:+Principles+and+Applications+kisaalita&pg=PP1}}</ref> His secondary line of research is in [[biogas]]-powered cooling of milk and other perishables in low-resource settings with no access to electricity.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://psmag.com/kisaalita-engineers-solutions-for-africa-s-rural-poor-74e12934f6ae#.5rsh0ik9h|title=Kisaalita Engineers Solutions for Africa's Rural Poor|publisher=}}</ref> His research areas include the following:
* Tissue engineering
* Cell-surface interactions
* Assays for high throughput screening (HTS)
* Renewable energy utilization with emphasis on biogas-powered cooling
* Global service learning

His work has been supported by several organizations including the [[Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://gcgh.grandchallenges.org/grant/designing-female-ergonomic-and-cultural-appropriateness|title=Designing for Female Ergonomic and Cultural Appropriateness - Grand Challenges|website=gcgh.grandchallenges.org}}</ref> [[World Bank]], the [[National Science Foundation]], the [[U.S. Department of Agriculture]], and the [[United States Environmental Protection Agency|Environmental Protection Agency]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://psmag.com/kisaalita-engineers-solutions-for-africa-s-rural-poor-74e12934f6ae#.j96yx0wfx|title=Kisaalita Engineers Solutions for Africa's Rural Poor|publisher=}}</ref>

== Awards ==
* 2016 University of Georgia's President's Fulfilling the Dream Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://news.uga.edu/releases/article/2016-presidents-fulfilling-dream-award/|title=UGA presents 2016 President's Fulfilling the Dream Award|date=22 January 2016|publisher=}}</ref>
* 2015 Lioba Moshi Award for Service in African Studies.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineering.uga.edu/newsroom/news/kisaalita-receives-african-studies-award|title = UGA College of Engineering| date=9 November 2015 }}</ref>
* 2015 University of Georgia College of Engineering's Distinguished Faculty Scholar Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.engineering.uga.edu/newsroom/news/hornak-kisaalita-receive-distinguished-faculty-scholar-award|title = UGA College of Engineering| date=28 May 2015 }}</ref>
* 2015 University of Georgia Richard Reiff Internationalization Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://international.uga.edu/about/news/78-uga-faculty-and-staff-receive-awards-from-the-office-of-international-education|title=Home|access-date=2016-10-03|archive-date=2017-09-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170907214747/https://international.uga.edu/about/news/78-uga-faculty-and-staff-receive-awards-from-the-office-of-international-education|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2013 Powering Agriculture Award: An Energy Grand Challenge for Development initiative.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://poweringag.org/news-events/video/william-kisaalita-winning-2013-award|title=William Kisaalita on Winning a 2013 Powering Agriculture Award - Powering Agriculture|website=poweringag.org|access-date=2016-10-03|archive-date=2020-08-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200810213556/https://poweringag.org/news-events/video/william-kisaalita-winning-2013-award|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2008 University of Georgia Scholarship of Engagement Award.<ref name="uga.edu">{{cite web|url=http://news.uga.edu/releases/article/engineering-professor-named-associate-director-of-curo/|title=Engineering professor named associate director of Center for Undergraduate Research Opportunities|date=12 August 2011|publisher=}}</ref>
* 2004 University Mentor of the Year for Undergraduate Research, University of Georgia Honors Program.<ref name="uga.edu"/>
* 2002 Lowry H. Gillespie, Jr. Award.<ref name="uga.edu"/>
